strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas GH#68315 (wrong float->Int64 conversion in Series.convert_dtypes for out-of-int64-range floats, plus spurious RuntimeWarning) by installing pandas from a known buggy commit and running the specific failing test(s) added/modified in pandas/tests/series/methods/test_convert_dtypes.py. The test expects out-of-range floats/±inf to convert to Float64 with no warnings, and float(INT_MAX+1) to fall back to Float64 rather than producing an off-by-one Int64.

system_packages: (build tooling for compiling pandas extensions, e.g. gcc/clang and python headers)
build_commands: python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pip install . --no-build-isolation  # for deps present in environment, if needed
pinned_because: Exact pandas revision is required: BUGGY COMMIT 7d79fc449944 must be checked out; the fix is in a later revision and the test must switch from failing to passing across that transition.

The reproduction relies on pandas core casting behavior in convert_dtypes and downcasting helpers; using the repo’s exact source tree (editable install) ensures the test exercises that revision’s code.

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision 7d79fc449944: the selected test(s) fail because convert_dtypes either (1) emits a RuntimeWarning for out-of-range floats/±inf despite tm.assert_produces_warning(None), and/or (2) incorrectly returns an Int64/incorrect value for float(INT_MAX+1) instead of falling back to Float64. On fixed revision (the PR containing the floats_fit_integer_dtype guard): the same test(s) pass with no warnings and with dtype fallback to Float64 when values do not fit in int64 bounds.
strategy.numerical_probe: The test asserts dtype/value equality via tm.assert_series_equal, not by manually inspecting numerical scalars. It specifically targets the buggy cast path where an unguarded (arr.astype(int) == arr).all() can become true due to saturating cast behavior for out-of-range floats.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: returns dtype Int64 with stored value 9223372036854775807
input_output_examples.expected_output: should not convert to Int64; should fall back to Float64 (exact numeric Float64 output not specified in provided evidence)

risks: Platform/toolchain dependency: the test_convert_dtypes_float_one_past_max derives bounds from np.dtype(int) (platform C int). As noted in the test, the cast is to the platform’s C int; if the buggy behavior differs across 32-bit vs 64-bit builds, the failing value might change or the path might not reproduce identically.

Warnings behavior sensitivity: the reproduction relies on tm.assert_produces_warning(None) catching a RuntimeWarning. If warning emission is suppressed differently by the runtime or compile flags, the assertion could pass even if the dtype is still wrong.

Architecture-specific casting: the described saturating cast behavior from float to int may differ by platform/ABI; if the issue only triggers on certain architectures, you may need to run on the same architecture as the bug report (not specified in evidence).

oracle.why: The expected outputs are constructed in the test using ser.astype('Float64') (and ser.astype('Int64') for an unaffected minimum case), so equality is exact within those dtypes.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: For the buggy commit 7d79fc449944, at least one of the selected tests fails: (a) tm.assert_produces_warning(None) fails because a RuntimeWarning is raised for out-of-range floats (e.g., 1e30, ±inf), and/or (b) tm.assert_series_equal fails because convert_dtypes incorrectly accepts a float as integral and returns an Int64 (off-by-one for float(INT_MAX+1)), rather than falling back to ser.astype('Float64').
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed pandas revision that adds the floats_fit_integer_dtype guard before the integrality check in convert_dtypes, the selected tests pass: no RuntimeWarning is produced and the results exactly match ser.astype('Float64') for out-of-range/±inf and float(INT_MAX+1), while float(iinfo.min) still converts to Int64 as expected.
